humanities_role_explanation: SuperGPQA is a general graduate-level knowledge and reasoning benchmark across 285 subfields, dominated by STEM (Science, Engineering, Medicine = 77.2%). Humanities subsets (History 674, Literature and Arts 1,676, Philosophy 347) supply items, but the competence tested is generic multiple-choice knowledge/reasoning, not humanities-specific interpretive competence.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text-only multiple-choice questions; image-dependent questions were explicitly excluded via a multimodal exclusion step.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Graduate-level multiple-choice questions with about 10 options; 42.33% require mathematical calculation or formal reasoning. Humanities items (e.g., dance studies statements, Ross's prima facie duties, history, musicology) are largely factual/conceptual recall in MCQ format. The paper describes the hard split as testing reasoning and easy/middle splits as testing factual knowledge mastery.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Broad multi-discipline benchmark covering 13 disciplines, 72 fields and 285 subfields.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Evaluates 6 reasoning, 28 chat and 17 base models including DeepSeek-R1, o1, o3-mini, GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Gemini-2.0-flash, Qwen2.5, Llama-3.1, Mistral.

quantitative_metrics.note: Accuracy at sample, subfield, field and discipline levels; plus SD, CV and high-low discrimination indices.

summary: SuperGPQA is a 26,529-question multiple-choice benchmark spanning 285 graduate-level disciplines, built via a human-LLM collaborative pipeline with expert source screening, crowd transcription and three-stage quality inspection. Evaluation of 51 LLMs shows substantial headroom, with DeepSeek-R1 best at 61.82% accuracy.
key_findings: DeepSeek-R1 reaches 61.82% overall accuracy, o1-2024-12-17 60.24%. Reasoning models lead; instruction tuning helps greatly (DeepSeek-V3 47.40 vs. base 32.14). Stronger models are more balanced across difficulty. History (CV=0.175, Δ=19.19) and Law are the most discriminating disciplines; History and Literature & Arts have the lowest mean accuracy (48.28, 46.94).
facets_explanation: Experts selected credible source questions (textbook example problems with solutions, exercise websites) and crowd annotators (undergraduate/master students) transcribed, translated and converted them to MCQs, with LLM-generated distractors checked by annotators; experts with PhD or pursuing PhD re-annotated suspicious items. Majority of answers thus come from existing textbook/exam-style solutions. Each item has exactly one correct option, and annotators were told to avoid regional bias.
results_explanation: Table 5: DeepSeek-R1 61.82 overall (sample) accuracy. Difficulty gap: Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct scores 44.82 on easy vs 19.97 on hard; Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct 48.22 vs 15.22 (33 points); GPT-4o-2024-11-20 56.84 vs 23.50 (33); Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct-style largest gap is claude-3-5-sonnet 59.04 vs 29.99 (29), and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct 32.82 vs 7.22 (26); the largest gap is Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-free: Qwen2.5-72B base 46.20 vs 15.01 (31) and Llama-3.1-70B 40.78 vs 12.78; maximum taken as roughly 37 from Qwen2.5-14B-style comparisons across Table 12 (e.g. gemma-2-9b-it 37.81 vs 10.60 = 27; Qwen-max-2025 58.16 vs 33.09 = 25), so this figure is approximate. Subfield prompt input comparison shows small differences (<1.2 points). No human baseline reported.
